item.title: The US election could turn the country into chaos
item.description: Trump already tried to overturn one election he lost. On November 3, he’s likely to lose another one, badly. At this point it is obvious to almost everybody that the Republican Party, and thus Trump, is going to get smashed in the midterms. Chances are that both the House and the Senate will be flipped. A year ago, it was mostly unthinkable that the Democrats could flip the Senate. Although it would be a massive loss, even for a midterm, in this post I want to make the point that this is not just another election. Trump doesn’t like to lose I don’t think Trump would take this loss lightly, especially after a potential landslide. I think Trump will challenge, litigate and threaten to get the result of the election overturned, at least in key states. Some of the litigation has already started. When I mention this to folks, so far everyone replies with skepticism: they don’t think that could happen, or that it’s even possible. To me this is a clear example of normalcy bias, and it’s quite easy to show why: Trump has already tried to overturn an election that he lost, in 2020. To this day, he doesn’t admit that he lost that election, and neither do key members of his cabinet. That alone should have been a massive red flag against voting for him in 2024, but here we are anyway and it’s about to happen again1. There is speculation that the administration will try to influence the elections by using force, but as this excellent piece from Nate Silver’s newsletter describes, it may not even be possible to do at scale, although they might pull it off in a specific key race. Even if it doesn’t happen, the fact that we’re talking about it at all says a lot about how unstable things could get. Many people think that he doesn’t admit he lost because he genuinely believes he won. The case for unfitness is the same either way: either he ignored the popular vote to stay in power unlawfully, or he was delusional (or dumb) enough to reject a clear reality. ↩
